solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: College failure becomes a pitcher

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for college
a failure is a loser

explanation.surface: A student who flunks out of college ends up as a jug, or as a baseball player.
explanation.walkthrough: In baseball a closer is the relief pitcher sent in to finish off a game; 'pitcher' tempts you towards a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: In American baseball the closer is the specialist relief thrower brought on for the final innings.

clue.text: Memorable girl wanted at home about to board

indicators.note: to board something is to get inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Cathy Come Home is the 1966 Ken Loach TV play, so the girl wanted at home is Cathy
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: An unforgettable girl is missed by her family and should come home.
explanation.walkthrough: Cathy Come Home was a famous BBC drama about homelessness; its title tells you the girl who is wanted at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchy tune or slogan is one that sticks easily in the mind.

clue.text: Job of no consequence in Ireland! Little work and, gosh, I toil hard

definitions.text: Job of no consequence in Ireland
definitions.note: the clue gives the job; the answer is the person who does it

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: worked hard, these letters are knocked out of their order and reshaped

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a pointless Irish job while toiling away.
explanation.walkthrough: St Patrick is said to have driven the snakes out of Ireland, so a snake expert there would have nothing to study.
explanation.definitionFit: An ophiologist studies snakes, and Ireland famously has none, so the post would be of no consequence there.

clue.text: Answer is to go up with string to join pipes the old way

definitions.text: to join pipes the old way

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading these words from the bottom to the top

parts.note: A is the usual abbreviation for answer
taken as written
the mese is the middle string of the ancient Greek lyre

explanation.surface: An instruction about running a pipe upwards and tying it with string.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers gives siamese as a verb, to join pipes or the like, now old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, siamese once meant to connect things together like conjoined twins, used especially of pipes.

clue.text: Guard clearing right of access for that reason

indicators.note: clearing something away removes it from the word it sits in

parts.note: a sentry guards a post

indicators.note: the right-hand end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A guard clears the way, giving someone right of entry for a good reason.
explanation.walkthrough: The word access works twice: its last letter is the one removed, and it is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Entry and access both mean the means or right of getting in.

clue.text: What's left I used freely in base of daquiri

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a daiquiri is a cocktail based on rum

indicators.note: used freely, these letters are not held to their order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A drinker confesses to pouring freely into the bottom of a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: Base here means the main spirit of the drink, not the bottom of the glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A residuum is a residue, the part remaining after the rest is gone.

clue.text: Brown would be excluded if opening with book

indicators.note: asks what the word would be if a different letter began it

parts.note: excluded means banned
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A brown book might be banned, the clue seems to hint.
explanation.walkthrough: Read in reverse: the answer, with its first letter swapped for B, becomes the word for excluded.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanned skin has gone brown in the sun, so tanned works as the adjective brown.

clue.text: Take up difficulty over point

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
PT is the abbreviation for point

explanation.surface: Someone takes up a dispute over a particular point.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt an idea or cause is to take it up and make it your own.

clue.text: Rare goose caught by inhumane neighbour

indicators.note: something caught by the following words is held within them

parts.note: runs across the join between the two words

explanation.surface: A cruel neighbour has snatched an endangered goose.
explanation.definitionFit: The nene is the Hawaiian goose, once close to extinction and still rare.

clue.text: Put out by online fault? Time to enter "delete"

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: an e-vice: e- for electronic or online, plus a vice or fault
T is the abbreviation for time
D is short for delete, as in proof-reading

explanation.surface: Someone is thrown off a website for a fault, and it is time to press delete.
explanation.walkthrough: E-VICE is a playful coinage: the e- prefix marks anything done online.
explanation.definitionFit: Evicted means forced out of a home, which is to be put out.

clue.text: Faff about Rimbaud's named successor (in short in Latin)

parts.note: Rimbaud wrote French, and dit is French for named or called
her. is the abbreviation of Latin heres, heir

explanation.surface: A literary query about who the poet Rimbaud named as his heir.
explanation.walkthrough: Faff is British slang for fussing without getting anything done.
explanation.definitionFit: To faff about is to dither, wavering indecisively instead of acting.

clue.text: Gardeners near their peak delight in these trees on a lake

definitions.text: Gardeners near their peak delight in these

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for lake
pines are conifers

explanation.surface: Mountain gardeners admire trees growing beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'trees on a lake' puts the trees after the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpines are small mountain plants, prized by rock gardeners, and the gardeners near a peak would grow them.

clue.text: Yes, great pal is excited to make the final entrance?

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up, so these letters are agitated into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A friend gets excited about making a grand last entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: The pearly gates are the traditional gates of heaven, the doorway one passes through after death.

clue.text: Whoops! I tend to flounder round boaters, or similar

indicators.note: going round something encloses it
to flounder is to thrash about clumsily, throwing these letters into disorder

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
boaters are straw hats

explanation.surface: Someone admits they keep floundering when rowing near boats.
explanation.walkthrough: Boaters look like rowers on the river; they are flat straw hats.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of dismay when something goes wrong.

clue.text: Eg, Bravo Charlie … Romeo by instant messaging

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
IM is the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: A string of radio alphabet words sent by text message.
explanation.walkthrough: Bravo looks like another radio letter, but here it means a hired thug or desperado.
explanation.definitionFit: A bravo is a villain hired to do violence, so he is an example of a criminal, informally a crim.

clue.text: Charge one's own claim to being a doozy

parts.note: saying I'M is claiming to be something yourself
a peach is something outstanding, like a doozy

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of boasting that they are a real stunner.
explanation.walkthrough: Doozy is American slang for an outstanding example; the whole wordplay says 'I'm a peach'.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach a public official is to charge them formally with misconduct.

clue.text: Rhubarb and honey — mean to be ordinary

indicators.note: the mean is the middle, and to be something else means that middle letter is swapped out

parts.note: taken as written
O is the abbreviation for ordinary

explanation.surface: A recipe pairing rhubarb with honey, made ordinary and plain.
explanation.walkthrough: Mean suggests stingy or average; here it is the middle letter. Rhubarb is British slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb and hooey are both slang for nonsense or empty talk.

clue.text: Contemplation about one's wasting

indicators.note: something placed about another surrounds it

parts.note: musing is quiet contemplation
one is I, and 's is is

explanation.surface: A reflection on how a person's time is being wasted.
explanation.definitionFit: Misusing resources means using them wrongly, which is wasting them.

clue.text: Cake for broadcaster from Dublin

parts.note: to can stand for for, as in the key to the door
RTE is Ireland's national broadcaster, based in Dublin

explanation.surface: A cake intended for an Irish TV presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' looks like a link word, but it supplies the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A torte is a rich layered cake of central European style.

clue.text: Downy, in the manner of Wodehouse you might say

parts.note: P. G. Wodehouse was nicknamed Plum
the adjective ending -ose means having the quality of

explanation.surface: A fluffy writing style is said to be Wodehousian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you might say' admits that 'Plum-ose' for Wodehouse-like is a jokey coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumose means feathery, covered in fine down like a plume.

clue.text: Question for right solver who enjoys trifles

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'one who', the noun

indicators.note: putting one thing for another means swapping it in its place

parts.note: QU is an abbreviation for question
R is the abbreviation for right
a riddler is one who reads or solves riddles

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter's query about the right solver for someone who likes desserts.
explanation.walkthrough: Trifles suggests the British layered pudding; here it means trivial things.
explanation.definitionFit: To quiddle is to trifle or fuss over trivia, so a quiddler is a person who does that.

clue.text: Uni lads developing explosive mixtures

indicators.note: developing things change shape as they grow, so these letters take a new form

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: University students cooking up something dangerous in the lab.
explanation.definitionFit: Dualin is an explosive made of nitroglycerine absorbed in sawdust, one of the dynamite family.

clue.text: Soppiness about old English black plant

indicators.note: something placed about another wraps round it

parts.note: slush is mawkish sentimentality
O is the abbreviation for old
E is the abbreviation for English
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Sentimentality about an old English plant with black fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black plant' reads as one phrase, fitting the dark sloe, but black only gives a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The sloe bush is the blackthorn, a shrub that bears sloes.

clue.text: In due course joey will be stoked to get diluted soda etc

parts.note: so in the sense of then or next, as in 'and so to bed'

indicators.note: stoking a fire stirs it up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A young kangaroo will eventually be thrilled with a fizzy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A joey is a baby kangaroo, and stoked is Australian slang for delighted; here stoked means stirred.
explanation.definitionFit: Soojey is a sailor's cleaning solution of soda, soap and water for scrubbing paintwork.

clue.text: Clock wherein you see trailer

indicators.note: something seen within another sits inside it

parts.note: clock is slang for face
a trailer is an advert for a film

explanation.surface: A clock face carrying a film advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken whole, the clue describes a front put up for show, carrying a promotion: that showy front is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A facade is the front face of a building, often a showy exterior that advertises more than lies behind.

clue.text: Anything or, for a few, nothing is accepted without opening

indicators.note: lacking its opening means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: nought is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A puzzling statement that some people accept anything, or nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Ought is an old form of aught, anything; a few speakers also use it for nought, which is the joke in 'or, for a few, nothing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ought is a variant of aught, an archaic word for anything at all.

clue.text: Hat to leak

parts.note: taken as written
a leak is slang for urinating

explanation.surface: A hat that lets the rain through.
explanation.walkthrough: To take a leak is slang for to urinate.
explanation.definitionFit: A topee is a lightweight pith helmet worn as a sun hat in the tropics.

clue.text: Parent on dog's well-defined bit of body

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow or tag along
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A parent leaning over the dog's sharply defined body part.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'Parent on dog' puts the parent after the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A tagma is one of the distinct body regions of an arthropod, such as the head, thorax or abdomen.

clue.text: Raja in a state of drought starts to kick up

parts.note: a tun is the shrivelled dormant state a tardigrade enters when dried out

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters

parts.note: the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A ruler kicks up a fuss when his land is suffering drought.
explanation.walkthrough: Tardigrades (water bears) survive drying out by curling into a tun; 'tun' as a barrel is the false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunku is a title for a prince in the Malay states, a ruler like an Indian raja.

clue.text: Odd form of compulsion finds this minatory PLC fazed

indicators.note: an odd form is a strange rearrangement of the letters
sounds like phased, as in phased out, so these letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
the letters taken away

explanation.surface: A company is rattled by a strange, threatening compulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: PLC (public limited company) looks like the fazed victim, but its letters are struck out of the long word.
explanation.definitionFit: Minatory and ominous both describe something threatening or foreboding.

clue.text: Supplier of aromatic remedies is born with millions

parts.note: née means born, used before a maiden name
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A natural medicine company is born and makes millions.
explanation.definitionFit: The neem is an Indian tree whose bitter oil and bark are used in traditional medicine.

clue.text: I'm no pro — in short, against avoiding brief

indicators.note: avoiding something means leaving it out

parts.note: laconic means using few words
con is against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: An amateur admits, briefly, that they're against short answers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pro' and 'against' make you think of pros and cons; pro here is a professional.
explanation.definitionFit: A laic is a layman, someone outside the clergy or a profession, and so no professional.

clue.text: Who was famously refused gets it in? It's occasionally unearthed

indicators.note: getting something in places it inside

parts.note: 'Not tonight, Josephine' is the line attributed to Napoleon
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spurned lover finally gets lucky, then something rarely comes to light.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator includes the inserted word itself: 'gets it in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Josephinite is a rare nickel-iron mineral found as pebbles in Josephine County, Oregon, so only now and then dug up.

clue.text: Canned in Queensland adopting not forgotten way to stand

definitions.note: an adjective describing a way of standing

indicators.note: adopting something takes it in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: inked is Australian slang for drunk, or canned
ne is an obsolete word for not

explanation.surface: Something tinned in Queensland takes on an unforgettable posture.
explanation.walkthrough: Canned means drunk; Queensland signals Australian slang.
explanation.definitionFit: In-kneed means knock-kneed, with the knees bent inwards, describing how someone stands.

clue.text: Republic succeeded drawing in obsequious sorts

indicators.note: drawing something in pulls it inside

parts.note: Yemen is a republic in Arabia
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: A republic did well by attracting fawning followers.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes-men agree with everything their superior says, which makes them servile flatterers.

clue.text: The herpetologist Fink-Nottle in differing guises?

indicators.note: differing forms of a word have their letters in a different order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Wodehouse newt-fancier appears in various disguises.
explanation.walkthrough: Gussie Fink-Nottle is the newt-obsessed friend of Bertie Wooster in P. G. Wodehouse's comic novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustus 'Gussie' Fink-Nottle keeps and studies newts, making him a reptile-and-amphibian enthusiast by first name.
